previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex history of sclerosing mesenteritis, recurrent small bowel obstruction, and 23 prior abdominal surgeries was admitted for management of chronic abdominal pain and new-onset subjective orthostatic dizziness. She received her established ED pain protocol with IV Dilaudid and IV fluids for dehydration. Evaluation revealed no acute infection or cardiopulmonary process. Her dizziness was not fully explained by orthostatic vital signs but was likely related to recent dose increases in clonidine and Abilify. The decision was made to reduce Abilify to her prior dose of 2 mg daily, with close follow-up recommended. Her abdominal pain remained at baseline, and she continued home TPN. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to monitor symptoms and follow up with her primary care and psychiatric providers.

#Chronic abdominal pain/Small bowel obstruction:
Patient was placed on wall suction through her G-tube and had 
large volume output of fecal material over the entirety of her 
hospital stay. She was seen by general surgery as well as the 
attending surgeon who had operated on her in the past and she 
felt that there was no surgical intervention to be offered to 
the patient and that her risk of volvulus was very low given the 
degree of adhesions.  Pain control has been extraordinarily 
difficult to achieve with this patient and while in-patient an 
in depth discussion with her outpatient pain, GI and primary 
care providers were initiated.  The patient was offered both 
long term nursing and hospice placement, but declined both as 
she felt too young.  An inpatient pain consult was placed that 
did not provide signifcantly new approach to her pain control, 
but recommended Diluadid PR as an outpatient.  While in house 
the patient was given Diluaid 1 mg in 100 cc of NS over 1 hour 
q6h with some pain control, but no resolution in pain.  Patient 
also recieved IV phenergan 12.5 mg x2 every 6 hours as needed 
for nausea.  A discharge plan of Liquid Phenergan 12.5 mg every 
___s 3 mg diluadid PR Q3H:PRN was arrived at.  All 
of her home medications were continued while inpaitent.

INDICATION:  ___ with abdominal pain.  Please assess for obstruction.

TECHNIQUE:  Total of four both supine and upright views of the abdomen were
obtained.

COMPARISON:  CT of the abdomen from ___.  Abdominal radiograph
from ___.  

FINDINGS:  There are multiple air-fluid levels and dilated segments of small
bowel, similar to ___, potentially due to chronic small-bowel
obstruction but not significantly changed allowing for differences in
technique.  There is no evidence of free air.  Also seen is a right femoral
line ending in the hepatic IVC and a pigtail catheter projecting over the
right upper quadrant.

IMPRESSION:  Similar bowel dilatation, which may reflect chronic partial
obstruction; mild distension of the colon however suggests that there may also
be component of dysmotility.
